prompt: Draw a study corner in isometric projection, as a single self-contained SVG. A wooden floor meets two walls; against them stand a tall bookshelf and a desk. The bookshelf's four shelves carry books three ways at once: rows standing upright, a pair leaning over at the end of a row, and small piles lying flat. On the desk a lamp burns and throws a pool of warm light across the wood, beside a mug and a potted plant. On the floor in front of the desk a cat sleeps curled on a round cushion. The projection must be true rather than suggested: every vertical edge is vertical on screen, every other straight edge runs on one of the two isometric diagonals, a gizmo states the three axes, every shadow is thrown the same way by a single light, every object rests on the surface that supports it, and the scene is painted strictly back to front.
definition_of_done: final_output_file: isometric-study.svg, a single self-contained SVG. All 14 cases in test_acceptance.py pass via `python -I -m unittest discover -s . -v` with exit code 0. 1. The file parses as XML, the root is <svg>, and its viewBox holds 4 numbers describing a frame at least 100 by 100. 2. Elements carry exactly these ids: study, backdrop, floor, floor-plane, wall-left, wall-right, shadows, bookshelf, shelf-1, shelf-2, shelf-3, shelf-4, books-upright, books-leaning, books-stacked, desk, desk-top, lamp, lamp-light, lamp-bulb, mug, plant, cushion, cushion-top, cat, cat-body, iso-axes, axis-x, axis-y, axis-z. 3. The file makes zero external requests: no http(s) href or src, no @import, no url(//...). 4. It contains no <script>, no <image> and no <foreignObject>. 5. The isometric frame holds everywhere it is claimed: outside any data-iso="off" subtree there is no <rect>, and every straight edge of every <polygon>, <polyline> and <line> runs within 1 degree of 30, 90 or 150 degrees on screen; at least 200 such edges are measured, so the frame is carried by a built scene and not by a handful of shapes. 6. The gizmo states the convention the drawing is built on: axis-x runs at 30 degrees, axis-y at 150, axis-z at 90, each is a single straight <line>, and the three foreshorten equally, their lengths agreeing within 2%. 7. Depth is declared and obeyed: at least 8 parts carry a numeric data-depth painter key, and their document order is non-decreasing in that key, so the scene paints back to front. 8. One light only: at least 4 elements carry data-anchor-x and data-anchor-y naming the screen point their caster stands on, each sits more than 1 unit from that anchor, and the directions of all those offsets lie within 3 degrees of each other. 9. Nothing floats: the data-foot points of bookshelf, desk and cushion all lie inside the #floor-plane polygon, and the data-foot points of lamp, mug and plant all lie inside the #desk-top polygon. 10. #books-upright holds at least 12 elements with class="book", and each one's drawn outline is taller on screen than it is wide, so it is standing rather than lying. 11. #books-stacked holds at least 4 elements with class="book", each wider on screen than it is tall, and their tops span more than 5 units, so books genuinely sit on other books. 12. #books-leaning holds at least 2 elements with class="book", and each one's most upright edge leans between 5 and 55 degrees away from vertical, so it is neither standing straight nor fallen flat. 13. The lamp lights the desk: #lamp-light is filled with a gradient defined in the same file, its centre lies inside the #desk-top polygon, and #lamp-bulb sits above that centre and within one pool radius of it horizontally. 14. The cat sleeps on the cushion: #cat's data-foot lies inside the #cushion-top ellipse, and #cat-body is at least 1.3 times as wide as it is tall, so the animal reads as curled and low. If the contract cannot be satisfied, return status='failure' with the precise reason rather than a partial drawing or a file that dodges the tests.
contract: Produce ONE SVG document in the `code` field, starting with <svg and ending with </svg>. The root <svg> needs xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" and a viewBox. Project with a single stated convention and state it in the drawing: screen y grows downward, sx = cx + (x - y) * cos30 * s, sy = cy + (x + y) * 0.5 * s - z * s, so +x runs 30 degrees down-right, +y runs 30 degrees down-left and +z runs straight up. #iso-axes holds three <line> elements, axis-x, axis-y and axis-z, drawn one unit long from a common origin, which is how the tests read the convention back. Tag the semantic parts with these exact ids: study (the whole scene group), backdrop, floor, floor-plane (the floor's ground quad), wall-left, wall-right, shadows, bookshelf, shelf-1, shelf-2, shelf-3, shelf-4, books-upright, books-leaning, books-stacked, desk, desk-top (the desk's top face), lamp, lamp-light, lamp-bulb, mug, plant, cushion, cushion-top, cat, cat-body, iso-axes, axis-x, axis-y, axis-z. All isometric geometry is drawn as <polygon>, <polyline> or <line> with raw numeric coordinates: no <rect>, because an axis-aligned rectangle can never be an isometric face. Anything genuinely off the isometric frame - the flat backdrop, a leaning book, a lamp shade, a curved mug, plant, cushion or cat - must sit inside a group carrying data-iso="off", which exempts it and everything below it from the angle check. Use that escape for what really is off-frame and nothing else. Every part of the scene that has a place in depth carries a numeric data-depth painter key, and parts appear in the document in non-decreasing data-depth order. Every object resting on something carries data-foot="x,y", the screen point where it meets its support: bookshelf, desk and cushion land on #floor-plane, lamp, mug and plant land on #desk-top, cat lands inside the #cushion-top ellipse. Every shadow carries data-anchor-x and data-anchor-y, the screen point its caster stands on, and the shadow's own centre (<polygon> centroid, or <ellipse> cx/cy) is displaced from that anchor. All those displacements must share one direction: one light, one shadow direction. Each individual book is an element with class="book" inside #books-upright, #books-leaning or #books-stacked, holding its own drawn faces. #lamp-light is an <ellipse> or <circle> with numeric cx, cy and rx (or r) filled with fill="url(#id)" referring to a gradient defined inline in <defs>; #lamp-bulb and #cushion-top likewise carry numeric cx/cy and rx/ry (or r), and #cat-body carries numeric rx/ry. Everything inline: no external fonts, no raster images, no scripts, no stylesheets, no network. Gradients, groups and opacity are fine, but no transform may move any measured geometry, since the tests read raw coordinates.

import math
import re
import unittest
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET
from pathlib import Path

TARGET = Path(__file__).resolve().parent / "isometric-study.svg"
REQUIRED_IDS = {"study", "backdrop", "floor", "floor-plane", "wall-left", "wall-right",
                "shadows", "bookshelf", "shelf-1", "shelf-2", "shelf-3", "shelf-4",
                "books-upright", "books-leaning", "books-stacked", "desk", "desk-top",
                "lamp", "lamp-light", "lamp-bulb", "mug", "plant", "cushion",
                "cushion-top", "cat", "cat-body", "iso-axes", "axis-x", "axis-y",
                "axis-z"}
# The only directions an isometric edge may take on screen, in degrees mod 180.
ISO_DIRECTIONS = (30.0, 90.0, 150.0)
ANGLE_TOL = 1.0
ON_DESK = ("lamp", "mug", "plant")
ON_FLOOR = ("bookshelf", "desk", "cushion")


def tag(el):
    return el.tag.split("}")[-1]


def num(value, default=None):
    try:
        return float(str(value).strip())
    except (TypeError, ValueError):
        return default


def pairs(points):
    """Every (x, y) in a points= attribute, whatever the separators."""
    parts = [p for p in re.split(r"[\s,]+", (points or "").strip()) if p]
    vals = [v for v in (num(p) for p in parts) if v is not None]
    return list(zip(vals[0::2], vals[1::2]))


def edges(el):
    """Every straight segment an element states in raw coordinates."""
    kind = tag(el)
    if kind in ("polygon", "polyline"):
        pts = pairs(el.get("points"))
        if len(pts) < 2:
            return []
        segs = list(zip(pts, pts[1:]))
        if kind == "polygon":
            segs.append((pts[-1], pts[0]))
        return segs
    if kind == "line":
        a = (num(el.get("x1")), num(el.get("y1")))
        b = (num(el.get("x2")), num(el.get("y2")))
        if None in a or None in b:
            return []
        return [(a, b)]
    return []


def direction(seg):
    """Screen angle of a segment in [0, 180), or None if it is too short to read."""
    (x1, y1), (x2, y2) = seg
    dx, dy = x2 - x1, y2 - y1
    if math.hypot(dx, dy) < 0.5:
        return None
    return math.degrees(math.atan2(dy, dx)) % 180.0


def off_vertical(seg):
    """How far a segment leans away from the vertical, in degrees."""
    a = direction(seg)
    return None if a is None else abs(90.0 - a)


def bbox(parts):
    pts = [pt for part in parts for pt in pairs(part.get("points"))]
    xs = [p[0] for p in pts]
    ys = [p[1] for p in pts]
    return min(xs), min(ys), max(xs), max(ys)


def inside(point, polygon):
    """Ray casting: is the point within the closed polygon?"""
    x, y = point
    hit = False
    n = len(polygon)
    for i in range(n):
        (x1, y1), (x2, y2) = polygon[i], polygon[(i + 1) % n]
        if (y1 > y) != (y2 > y):
            cut = x1 + (y - y1) * (x2 - x1) / (y2 - y1)
            if cut > x:
                hit = not hit
    return hit


class Acceptance(unittest.TestCase):
    @classmethod
    def setUpClass(cls):
        cls.raw = TARGET.read_text(encoding="utf-8")
        cls.root = ET.fromstring(cls.raw)
        cls.byid = {}
        cls.order = {}
        for i, el in enumerate(cls.root.iter()):
            ident = el.get("id")
            if ident and ident not in cls.byid:
                cls.byid[ident] = el
                cls.order[ident] = i
        box = (cls.root.get("viewBox") or "").replace(",", " ").split()
        cls.vb = [num(v) for v in box] if len(box) == 4 else [None] * 4

    # --- helpers ---------------------------------------------------------
    def node(self, ident):
        el = self.byid.get(ident)
        self.assertIsNotNone(el, "missing id=%s" % ident)
        return el

    def polygon(self, ident):
        pts = pairs(self.node(ident).get("points"))
        self.assertGreaterEqual(len(pts), 3,
                                "id=%s must carry a numeric points= outline" % ident)
        return pts

    def foot(self, ident):
        raw = self.node(ident).get("data-foot")
        self.assertIsNotNone(raw, "id=%s needs data-foot=\"x,y\"" % ident)
        pt = pairs(raw)
        self.assertEqual(len(pt), 1, "id=%s has a malformed data-foot=%r" % (ident, raw))
        return pt[0]

    def framed(self):
        """Every (element, in-frame?) pair, honouring inherited data-iso=off."""
        found = []

        def walk(el, live):
            live = live and (el.get("data-iso") != "off")
            found.append((el, live))
            for child in el:
                walk(child, live)

        walk(self.root, True)
        return found

    def books(self, ident):
        """Each book as the list of its drawn parts, so no segment is invented
        between one part and the next."""
        group = self.node(ident)
        out = []
        for el in group.iter():
            if el is group:
                continue
            if "book" in (el.get("class") or "").split():
                parts = [p for p in el.iter() if pairs(p.get("points"))]
                if parts:
                    out.append(parts)
        return out

    # --- structure -------------------------------------------------------
    def test_root_is_svg_with_viewbox(self):
        self.assertEqual(tag(self.root), "svg")
        self.assertNotIn(None, self.vb, "viewBox must have 4 numbers")
        w, h = self.vb[2], self.vb[3]
        self.assertTrue(w and w >= 100, "viewBox width too small: %r" % w)
        self.assertTrue(h and h >= 100, "viewBox height too small: %r" % h)

    def test_required_ids_present(self):
        missing = sorted(REQUIRED_IDS - set(self.byid))
        self.assertEqual(missing, [], "missing required ids: %s" % missing)

    def test_no_external_references(self):
        for el in self.root.iter():
            for key, value in el.attrib.items():
                if key.split("}")[-1] in ("href", "src") and re.match(r"\s*(https?:)?//", value or ""):
                    self.fail("external reference in %s: %s" % (tag(el), value))
        self.assertNotIn("@import", self.raw)
        self.assertFalse(re.search(r"url\(\s*['\"]?(https?:)?//", self.raw),
                         "external url() reference")

    def test_no_script_or_raster(self):
        kinds = {tag(el) for el in self.root.iter()}
        self.assertNotIn("script", kinds, "SVG must not contain <script>")
        self.assertNotIn("image", kinds, "SVG must be vector only, no <image>")
        self.assertNotIn("foreignObject", kinds)

    # --- the isometric frame ---------------------------------------------
    def test_every_edge_holds_the_isometric_frame(self):
        """Verticals stay vertical, everything else runs on one of the two
        isometric horizontals. Axis-aligned <rect>s cannot be isometric faces,
        so they are only allowed outside the frame."""
        counted = 0
        for el, live in self.framed():
            if not live:
                continue
            self.assertNotEqual(tag(el), "rect",
                                "a <rect> is axis-aligned and cannot be an isometric "
                                "face; put id=%r under data-iso=\"off\"" % el.get("id"))
            for seg in edges(el):
                angle = direction(seg)
                if angle is None:
                    continue
                counted += 1
                near = min(abs(angle - d) for d in ISO_DIRECTIONS)
                self.assertLessEqual(
                    near, ANGLE_TOL,
                    "edge %s in <%s id=%s> runs at %.2f deg, off the isometric "
                    "frame (allowed: %s)"
                    % (seg, tag(el), el.get("id"), angle, ISO_DIRECTIONS))
        self.assertGreaterEqual(counted, 200,
                                "only %d isometric edges: this is not a built scene"
                                % counted)

    def test_the_three_axes_agree_with_the_drawing(self):
        """The gizmo states the convention the whole drawing is built on."""
        lengths = {}
        for ident, want in (("axis-x", 30.0), ("axis-y", 150.0), ("axis-z", 90.0)):
            el = self.node(ident)
            seg = edges(el)
            self.assertEqual(len(seg), 1, "%s must be one straight <line>" % ident)
            angle = direction(seg[0])
            self.assertIsNotNone(angle, "%s has no measurable length" % ident)
            self.assertLessEqual(abs(angle - want), ANGLE_TOL,
                                 "%s runs at %.2f deg, expected %.1f deg"
                                 % (ident, angle, want))
            (x1, y1), (x2, y2) = seg[0]
            lengths[ident] = math.hypot(x2 - x1, y2 - y1)
        longest = max(lengths.values())
        for ident, length in lengths.items():
            self.assertLessEqual(abs(length - longest) / longest, 0.02,
                                 "%s is %.2f long against %.2f: the three unit axes "
                                 "must foreshorten equally" % (ident, length, longest))

    def test_objects_are_painted_back_to_front(self):
        """data-depth is the painter key; document order must follow it."""
        keys = []
        for el in self.root.iter():
            depth = num(el.get("data-depth"))
            if depth is not None:
                keys.append((depth, el.get("id")))
        self.assertGreaterEqual(len(keys), 8,
                                "only %d depth-keyed parts in the scene" % len(keys))
        order = [d for d, _ in keys]
        self.assertEqual(order, sorted(order),
                         "painted out of depth order: %s" % (keys,))

    def test_one_shadow_direction(self):
        """Every shadow is offset from its caster's anchor the same way."""
        vectors = []
        for el in self.root.iter():
            ax, ay = num(el.get("data-anchor-x")), num(el.get("data-anchor-y"))
            if ax is None or ay is None:
                continue
            pts = pairs(el.get("points"))
            if pts:
                cx = sum(p[0] for p in pts) / len(pts)
                cy = sum(p[1] for p in pts) / len(pts)
            else:
                cx, cy = num(el.get("cx")), num(el.get("cy"))
            self.assertIsNotNone(cx, "shadow <%s> has no measurable centre" % tag(el))
            length = math.hypot(cx - ax, cy - ay)
            self.assertGreater(length, 1.0,
                               "a shadow sits on its own anchor, so the light has "
                               "no direction: %s" % (el.attrib,))
            vectors.append(math.degrees(math.atan2(cy - ay, cx - ax)) % 360.0)
        self.assertGreaterEqual(len(vectors), 4,
                                "a lit scene needs at least 4 anchored shadows, got %d"
                                % len(vectors))
        spread = max(vectors) - min(vectors)
        self.assertLessEqual(spread, 3.0,
                             "shadows fall %.2f deg apart, so there is more than one "
                             "light: %s" % (spread, [round(v, 2) for v in vectors]))

    def test_objects_rest_on_their_supports(self):
        floor = self.polygon("floor-plane")
        desk = self.polygon("desk-top")
        for ident in ON_FLOOR:
            self.assertTrue(inside(self.foot(ident), floor),
                            "%s stands at %s, off the floor" % (ident, self.foot(ident)))
        for ident in ON_DESK:
            self.assertTrue(inside(self.foot(ident), desk),
                            "%s stands at %s, off the desk top"
                            % (ident, self.foot(ident)))

    # --- the shelves -----------------------------------------------------
    def test_upright_books_stand_taller_than_wide(self):
        shelved = self.books("books-upright")
        self.assertGreaterEqual(len(shelved), 12,
                                "a filled bookshelf needs >=12 upright books, got %d"
                                % len(shelved))
        for i, parts in enumerate(shelved):
            x0, y0, x1, y1 = bbox(parts)
            self.assertGreater(y1 - y0, x1 - x0,
                               "upright book %d measures %.1f wide by %.1f tall, so it "
                               "is not standing" % (i, x1 - x0, y1 - y0))

    def test_stacked_books_lie_flat(self):
        flat = self.books("books-stacked")
        self.assertGreaterEqual(len(flat), 4,
                                "need >=4 books stacked flat, got %d" % len(flat))
        for i, parts in enumerate(flat):
            x0, y0, x1, y1 = bbox(parts)
            self.assertGreater(x1 - x0, y1 - y0,
                               "stacked book %d measures %.1f wide by %.1f tall, so it "
                               "is not lying flat" % (i, x1 - x0, y1 - y0))
        tops = sorted(bbox(parts)[1] for parts in flat)
        self.assertGreater(tops[-1] - tops[0], 5.0,
                           "every flat book tops out at the same height, so nothing is "
                           "stacked on anything")

    def test_leaning_books_lean_out_of_the_frame(self):
        leaning = self.books("books-leaning")
        self.assertGreaterEqual(len(leaning), 2,
                                "need >=2 leaning books, got %d" % len(leaning))
        for i, parts in enumerate(leaning):
            segs = [s for part in parts for s in edges(part)]
            tilts = [t for t in (off_vertical(s) for s in segs) if t is not None]
            self.assertTrue(tilts, "leaning book %d has no measurable edge" % i)
            lean = min(tilts)
            self.assertTrue(5.0 <= lean <= 55.0,
                            "leaning book %d has its most upright edge %.2f deg off "
                            "vertical: it is either standing straight or fallen over"
                            % (i, lean))

    # --- the desk --------------------------------------------------------
    def test_the_lamp_casts_a_pool_of_light(self):
        pool = self.node("lamp-light")
        fill = (pool.get("fill") or "").strip()
        ref = re.match(r"url\(\s*#([^)\s]+)\s*\)", fill)
        self.assertIsNotNone(ref, "lamp-light must be filled with a gradient, got %r" % fill)
        self.assertIn(ref.group(1), self.byid,
                      "gradient #%s is never defined" % ref.group(1))
        px, py = num(pool.get("cx")), num(pool.get("cy"))
        rx = num(pool.get("rx"), num(pool.get("r")))
        self.assertIsNotNone(px, "lamp-light needs a numeric cx/cy")
        self.assertIsNotNone(rx, "lamp-light needs a numeric rx or r")
        self.assertTrue(inside((px, py), self.polygon("desk-top")),
                        "the pool of light at (%.1f, %.1f) does not land on the desk"
                        % (px, py))
        bulb = self.node("lamp-bulb")
        bx, by = num(bulb.get("cx")), num(bulb.get("cy"))
        self.assertIsNotNone(bx, "lamp-bulb needs a numeric cx/cy")
        self.assertLess(by, py, "the bulb at y=%.1f is not above its pool at y=%.1f"
                        % (by, py))
        self.assertLessEqual(abs(bx - px), rx,
                             "the bulb at x=%.1f is not over its pool at x=%.1f +/- %.1f"
                             % (bx, px, rx))

    def test_the_cat_sleeps_on_the_cushion(self):
        top = self.node("cushion-top")
        cx, cy = num(top.get("cx")), num(top.get("cy"))
        rx = num(top.get("rx"), num(top.get("r")))
        ry = num(top.get("ry"), num(top.get("r")))
        self.assertIsNotNone(cx, "cushion-top needs numeric cx/cy")
        self.assertIsNotNone(rx, "cushion-top needs numeric rx/ry")
        fx, fy = self.foot("cat")
        self.assertLessEqual(((fx - cx) / rx) ** 2 + ((fy - cy) / ry) ** 2, 1.0,
                             "the cat rests at (%.1f, %.1f), off the cushion" % (fx, fy))
        body = self.node("cat-body")
        brx = num(body.get("rx"), num(body.get("r")))
        bry = num(body.get("ry"), num(body.get("r")))
        self.assertIsNotNone(brx, "cat-body needs numeric rx/ry")
        self.assertGreaterEqual(brx, 1.3 * bry,
                                "cat-body is %.1f by %.1f: a sleeping cat is curled "
                                "and low, not upright" % (brx, bry))


if __name__ == "__main__":
    unittest.main()
